info.title: AIESS Analytics Tools
info.description: Energy monitoring, TGE pricing, chart generation, and rule history tools for the AIESS Energy Core agent.

get.description: Retrieves real-time battery status including SoC, PCS power, grid power, PV power, load, and the currently active rule from the last 2 minutes of telemetry data.
Retrieves aggregated energy statistics (averages of SoC, PCS power, grid power, PV power, load) for a specified time period. Auto-selects the optimal data bucket for the time range.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Number of hours to look back. Defaults to 24.

get.description: Retrieves TGE (Polish energy exchange) electricity prices. When hours is 0 or omitted, returns only the latest spot price. When hours > 0, returns a chart plus two structured digests `today` and `tomorrow`, each with: date, weekday, hourly[{hh_mm, price_pln_mwh, source}], min/max/avg, cheapest_hour, most_expensive_hour, cheapest_window, most_expensive_window. ALWAYS read these digests to know which prices belong to which day. NEVER infer the day from hh_mm alone — both today and tomorrow contain the same hours. The `source` field is `real` (settled auction price) or `predicted` (model forecast for hours not yet auctioned).

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Hours of price history to include each direction. Defaults to 0 (latest only). Use 24 to see today + tomorrow.

200.description: TGE electricity price data with today/tomorrow digests.

today.description: Digest for today: date, weekday, hourly, min/max/avg, cheapest_window, most_expensive_window.

tomorrow.description: Digest for tomorrow with the same structure as today. May have fewer hours if the day-ahead auction has not published all hours yet.

get.description: Retrieves rule history. Returns both config snapshots (what rules were configured in the shadow) and active rule execution history (which rule was actually running on the device firmware). Use type parameter to request only config, only active, or both. Always call this before speculating about which rule was active.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Number of hours to look back. Defaults to 24.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: History type: config, active, or both. Defaults to both.

get.description: Generates labeled datasets with time-series data points for visualization. Returns data formatted for line or bar charts. Available fields: grid_power, pcs_power, soc, total_pv_power, compensated_power. Use this when the user wants to see visual trends.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated field names: grid_power, pcs_power, soc, total_pv_power, compensated_power.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Number of hours to look back. Defaults to 24.

parameters.name: chart_type
parameters.description: Chart type: line or bar. Defaults to line.

200.description: Chart data with datasets and labels.

get.description: Retrieves PV production and load forecasts. Use this whenever the user asks about future energy production, PV forecast, jutro/tomorrow's production, expected load, or any forecast question. Returns a chart plus two structured digests `today` and `tomorrow`, each with: date, weekday, hourly[{hh_mm, pv_kw, load_kw}], pv_peak_kw, pv_peak_hour, pv_total_kwh, sunrise_kwh_hour, sunset_kwh_hour, load_peak_kw, load_peak_hour, net_surplus_kwh, net_deficit_kwh, avg_temp_c, avg_cloud_pct. ALWAYS narrate forecast values together with their date (e.g. 'jutro 21.05'). NEVER claim forecasting is unavailable — if you got a non-error response, the data is here. Forecast accuracy is ~10-15% (physics-based PV model + statistical load profile).

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Forecast horizon in hours. Defaults to 48. Use 48 for 'today + tomorrow' queries.
